messages.content: How can I sell my acoustic guitar?

function.name: tune_instrument
function.description: This function helps tune instruments based on the instrument type and the desired key or note. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

instrument_type.description: The type of the instrument, e.g. 'acoustic guitar', 'piano'.

key.description: The key or note to which the instrument should be tuned to. Default is 'Standard' for guitars.

message.content:
Here’s a step‑by‑step guide to help you get your acoustic guitar sold quickly and for a fair price: | Step | What to Do | Why It Matters | |------|------------|----------------| | **1. Clean & Tune** | Give the guitar a good wash, polish the finish, and tune it to standard pitch. | A well‑presented instrument looks more appealing and shows you’ve cared for it. | | **2. Take High‑Quality Photos** | Capture the body, neck, headstock, strings, and any imperfections from multiple angles. | Good photos attract buyers and reduce the chance of disputes over condition. | | **3. Research Market Value** | Check recent sales on Reverb, eBay, Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, and local music‑store listings. | Knowing the going rate helps you price competitively. | | **4. Write a Clear Listing** | Include brand, model, year, serial number, condition notes, and any accessories (case, strap, picks). | Transparency builds trust and speeds up negotiations. | | **5. Choose Your Platforms** | • **Reverb** – great for gear, offers buyer protection.
• **eBay** – wide audience, auction or fixed price.
• **Craigslist / Facebook Marketplace** – local, no shipping hassles.
• **Local Music Stores** – consignment or direct sale. | Different platforms reach different buyer types; use a mix for maximum exposure. | | **6. Set a Realistic Price** | Start slightly above your target to allow room for negotiation. | Buyers often expect to haggle; a higher starting point keeps you from underselling. | | **7. Decide on Shipping vs. Local Pickup** | If shipping, factor in packaging costs and insurance. For local pickup, meet in a safe, public place. | Shipping expands your market but adds cost; local pickup saves money and time. | | **8. Handle Negotiations Professionally** | Respond promptly, keep communication polite, and be prepared to justify your price with photos and market data. | Good communication can close the deal faster and avoid misunderstandings. | | **9. Finalize the Sale** | Use a secure payment method (PayPal, Venmo, cash, or a bank transfer). Sign a simple bill of sale if needed. | Protects both parties and provides a record of the transaction. | | **10. Ship or Deliver** | Package the guitar securely (bubble wrap, sturdy case, padded box). Track the shipment. | Reduces risk of damage and gives the buyer peace of mind. | ### Quick Tips - **Highlight Unique Features** – If your guitar has a special finish, custom inlay, or upgraded hardware, mention it. - **Offer Extras** – A case, strap, or a set of picks can sweeten the deal. - **Be Honest About Wear** – Disclose scratches, dents, or worn strings. Honesty builds buyer confidence. - **Use “As-Is” Wisely** – If you’re willing to accept a lower offer, state “as-is” but still provide accurate condition details. - **Safety First** – For in‑person meetings, choose a well‑lit, public location and consider bringing a friend. ### Example Listing (Reverb) ``` Title: 2015 Yamaha FG800 Acoustic Guitar – Excellent Condition Description: - Brand: Yamaha - Model: FG800 - Year: 2015 - Serial: 123456 - Finish: Natural - Condition: Minor scratch on back, no cracks, strings replaced last month - Accessories: Original case, strap, pick set - Notes: Tuned to standard EADGBE, ready to play Price: $350 (Negotiable) Photos: [Attach 5–6 high‑resolution images] Shipping: Ships within 3–5 business days, insured Payment: PayPal or Venmo ``` Feel free to adapt this template to your own guitar’s specifics. Good luck with the sale!
